thread.title: 3 Earnings Reports to Watch Next Week

author: InvestorPlace
title: 3 Earnings Reports to Watch Next Week
text:
Editor’s note: InvestorPlace’s Earnings to Watch is updated weekly. Please check back next week for our latest earnings calendar picks.
There are several key earnings reports on the earnings calendar next week. The obvious question is: will they matter?
For months now, there’s been a contradiction between steadily strong earnings reports and investor fears about external factors. Whether it’s tariffs and trade wars , higher interest rates and Treasury yields, or just valuation concerns, investors have been loath to embrace the bull market in 2018, even with solid results for most major companies.
InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading Tips
Over the past few weeks, those fears have taken center stage. The market has headed south. And while solid earnings reports gave the market a reprieve on Thursday, few investors are calling a bottom just yet.
So the question next week is whether good earnings can offset the fears driving stock prices down and volatility up. The good news is that there are a few huge reports next week. Tech titan Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) is among the heavies to report — but even given its size, in the context of this market, it’s not one of the most important reports.
8 'Greenlight' Stocks to Buy in a Sea of Red Three major companies struggling in various ways, for various reasons, will try and jumpstart a turnaround. And if these three earnings reports look good, they could go a long way toward convincing investors that more upside is ahead — for these three stocks and the market as a whole.
Earnings Reports: General Electric (GE) More
Source: Shutterstock
General Electric (GE) Earnings Report Date: Tuesday, Oct. 30, before market open
General Electric (NYSE: GE ) actually changed its earnings calendar for this report, pushing the release back by five days. The reason, as the company itself detailed , was to give new CEO Larry Culp more time to better understand the business.
Culp’s somewhat surprising hire at the beginning of the month gave a jolt to GE stock. But amid weakness in industrial stocks, GE stock again has faded. Tuesday morning’s report — and perhaps more importantly, the post-earnings conference call — will be the first step in restoring investor confidence.
To be sure, it’s unlikely that the report will contain any Earth-shattering news. Culp isn’t going to make major strategic changes after 30 days on the job. Still, GE’s actual numbers likely will be secondary to the new CEO’s take on the business. But long-suffering GE shareholders will be looking for any reason for hope — and perhaps some new ideas from Culp.
Few conference calls on any earnings calendar will be more widely listened to than the GE call on Tuesday morning.
Facebook (FB) More
Source: Shutterstock
Facebook (FB) Earnings Report Date: Tuesday, Oct. 30, after market close
The last time Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ) reported earnings, it led to the biggest one-day loss of market value in the history of the stock market. I wouldn’t expect quite the same level of fireworks on Tuesday afternoon — but this is a huge report for Facebook.
Confidence in the company has steadily eroded for much of the year. FB stock managed to recover from the Cambridge Analytica scandal back in March, but since then, the stock has given way. Q2 earnings disappointed, and the conference call was poorly executed. More issues are piling up . Executives are fleeing .
Everything here seems to be going in the wrong direction — including FB stock. Tuesday offers a chance to change that trajectory. Facebook stock still looks close to absurdly cheap given its growth, at less than 18x forward EPS estimates. A strong quarter — and strong commentary — that leads those analyst estimates higher gives FB a chance to rebound. Combined with a big quarter from Twitter (NYSE: TWTR ), it also changes the narrative around social media — and perhaps the online advertising space as a whole.
